lead: The money turns cautious: OpenAI halves its funding ambitions and Blackstone expects junk for Anthropic, while Wiz counts nine AI developer platforms breached in a single month.

sections.title: Capital gets selective
sections.intro: OpenAI trims its round from $30B to ~$20B at a lower valuation as investors cut commitments, Baseten more than doubles anyway, and the anchor of Anthropic's chip deal now expects a junk rating.

sections.title: The selloff, day two
sections.intro: Wall Street closes sharply lower again, with Amazon and Intel results deepening the AI cash-burn worries.

sections.title: A black October for AI platforms
sections.intro: Wiz connects nine breaches of AI developer platforms in one month - agent-swarm attack indications, distillation attempts, and one company shutting down.

sections.title: Rules of the road
sections.intro: OpenAI tightens weapons information for teens, and the four big labs back an IETF policy token so publishers can opt out of AI scraping once, for every crawler.

sections.title: The token mandate
sections.intro: Fortune's own account of Cisco handing a 27-year-old unlimited tokens to rewrite 98% of its legacy code - a bet against the graduate-hiring freeze.

sections.title: Chips and equity
sections.intro: Powerlattice nearly triples its funding to cut AI's power bill from inside the processor package.

sections.title: An NES in the weights
sections.intro: A working 6502 emulator baked into a 4B model, prompted into existence just for fun.
